chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they acquire from his delusions, as He the Exalted said: 'His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian and those who associate him [with Allah].'
ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over righteous believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's dominion is restricted to *al-dhann* (speculative delusions or minor heedlessness) rather than absolute control, preserving the believer's core faith. This distinction underscores the Shia theological view that while believers may fall into minor sins or distractions, they remain distinct from those who fully submit to Satan's will, as highlighted in the verse distinguishing between *shirk* and *dhann*. This nuanced understanding provides practical comfort, emphasizing that spiritual slip-ups do not equate to total loss of divine favor.
